# legacy-api

Generated by renvor as a **framework-backed starter**: a real Renvor application with the
kernel lifecycle, an HTTP server, persistence on postgres through sqlx, and no capabilities.
Every provider, route, and configuration key is in a file you own; nothing is hidden behind a
macro.

## Run

```
cp .env.example .env         # fill in every value; each is read from the environment only
$EDITOR .env
cargo run
```

`GET http://127.0.0.1:3000/` answers with the application's name. `renvor routes` and
`renvor openapi` inspect the same route registry the server serves, without a database.

## Where the framework comes from

`[framework]` in `renvor.toml` records the checkout every `path` dependency in `Cargo.toml`
points at, because no Renvor crate is published yet. When they are, each `path` becomes a
`version`. `Cargo.lock` was seeded from that checkout's lockfile, so this project resolves offline
on a machine that has built the framework.

## Configuration

One typed section per concern, each read lowest-precedence-first from its built-in defaults, its
optional `config/<section>.toml`, then the environment under `RENVOR_<SECTION>_…`. The
environment always wins, and every secret lives there and nowhere else — `.env.example` names
each one with an empty value. A value that is supplied and wrong stops the application at
**Validate**, naming the key, the constraint, and the layer, before a socket exists.

| Section | File | Secrets from the environment |
|---|---|---|
| `http` | `config/http.toml` | — |
| database | — | `RENVOR_DATABASE_URL` (the URL carries its credential: framework limitation 010/L-15, retained in Phase 011) |

## Persistence

Migrations under `migrations/` are applied **on Boot**, in version order, each checksummed, so an
edited migration fails closed rather than diverging silently. The directory holds the example
item migration — one directory, one
ledger.

## The generated test

`tests/starter.rs` proves this project the way the framework proves itself: it resets the
project's own tables and the migration ledger in the configured database, spawns the built binary, waits for readiness, drives it
over loopback HTTP and then, on unix, sends the interrupt a terminal would (`SIGINT`) and asserts a clean exit (status 0)
within the drain bound. On Windows a test cannot send that interrupt to a child, so there the test
ends the process and prints `SKIPPED:` for that one assertion rather than faking a clean exit
(the framework records this as Phase 011 limitation L-10); every other assertion runs on every platform.

```
RENVOR_DATABASE_URL=… cargo test
```

Without `RENVOR_DATABASE_URL` the test prints `SKIPPED` and passes, so `cargo test` works with no
services; set `RENVOR_TEST_REQUIRE_DATABASE=1` to make a skip a failure, which is what the
framework's own gate does.

## What this is not

A deployment. Secrets come from a file here and from a secret manager there; TLS to the backends
is off for loopback and on by default anywhere else; the limitations above are real. Renvor's
own limitations ledger says what it does not yet do, and this project inherits every line of it.
